0.text: How do i find my MAC adress ?

1.text: On which operatin system are you ?

2.text: Open the command prompt: press Windows + R, type cmd, then press Enter.

3.text:
In the command prompt, type ipconfig /all, then press Enter.
The information of all your network connections is displayed.

4.text:
Look for the line Physical Address: that's your MAC address (for example A4-83-E7-12-34-56).

If your computer has several network cards (wifi and Ethernet), each one has its own MAC address: make sure you note the one of the right connection.

answers.text: I can't find my MAC address

10.text: Click on the magnifier at the top right of your screen.

12.text: Write the following command : ifconfig and validate with Enter

13.text: Your MAC address is the value next to the entry ether (for example a4:83:e7:12:34:56). Several interfaces may be listed (en0, en1...): in that case, note each address with the name of its interface.

answers.text: I can't find my MAC address

20.text: Open a terminal. Depending on your distribution, it is called Terminal, Konsole, Xterm...

21.text:
Type ip link, then press Enter.
On older distributions, use ifconfig -a instead (or sudo ifconfig -a if access is denied).

22.text: Find the connection you are interested in (for example eth0 or enp… for Ethernet, wlan0 or wlp… for wifi). Your MAC address is the value next to link/ether (or ether / HWaddr with ifconfig).
